first_impression.reaction: The first paragraph gives me the shape of the day fast: speeches, fine mats, church, feast. Key takeaways name the siva and the taualuga but don't say what they are, so I had to scroll a long way on my phone to section 7 to find the dance.

journey.quote: It is the meeting of two families, carried out in the way of fa'a Samoa: chiefs and orators speak, fine mats change hands, the church blesses the marriage and the whole family sits down to eat.
journey.reaction: Okay, that's the answer to 'samoan wedding' in one sentence. Good start.

journey.quote: The church service sits at the heart of the day for many Samoan families, followed by speeches, the siva, the taualuga and a shared feast.
journey.reaction: I searched for the dance. This just lists two words I don't know. One more clause saying what the taualuga is would have saved me the scroll.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, Smartraveller advises Australians to "Exercise normal safety precautions" in Samoa, and an overseas marriage can't be registered in Australia, though it is usually recognised.
journey.reaction: I'm in Singapore and I wanted customs. Australian travel advice taking a whole takeaway feels off-topic.

journey.section: 1. Fa'a Samoa, matai and the families behind the wedding
journey.quote: Each aiga designates at least one matai to lead and represent it, and the matai form village councils that administer local affairs.
journey.reaction: Interesting, but this is the sixth paragraph of background before anything happens at the wedding. On the train I'm skimming past it.

journey.section: 3. Fine mats ('ie toga) and gifts between families
journey.quote: In Samoan marriage ceremonies, the bride's family presents 'ie toga to the husband's family.
journey.reaction: Clear, specific, sourced. That's the kind of fact I'd remember.

journey.section: 7. Siva Samoa and the taualuga: the Samoan dance at a wedding
journey.quote: At many Samoan weddings, the bride dances the taualuga to close the evening's formal dancing, while family members dance around her in support.
journey.reaction: This is what I came for, and the heading says exactly 'the Samoan dance at a wedding'. Love that. Just wish it were higher up and a bit longer.

journey.section: 7. Siva Samoa and the taualuga: the Samoan dance at a wedding
journey.quote: Couples planning the reception should give the taualuga its own moment in the running order, with the floor cleared and the music agreed with the family.
journey.reaction: Practical tip, short. Fine. But as a guest I still don't know what I'm supposed to do while she dances.

journey.section: 9. What UNESCO says about the 'ie Samoa
journey.quote: UNESCO describes the 'Ie Samoa as a finely hand-woven pandanus mat with two rows of green and red feathers at the hem, which can take up to several months and even years to make.
journey.reaction: Didn't section 3 already tell me the mats take months or years? Feels like the same thing twice.

journey.quote: What Are the Samoan Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
journey.reaction: Bit clickbaity, but the H2s underneath are clear, so it didn't stop me.

journey.quote: Dress as for church: a dress or blouse and skirt for women, trousers and a shirt for men.
journey.reaction: Useful FAQ, quick answers. The taualuga FAQ is there too. Next time I'd jump straight here.
